purpose: Does the 3.0.0 lean debugger text keep the zero-tool root-cause accuracy, F-code agreement and unsupported-claim rate of the 2.0.1 text on the 28 real failures of the v3 corpus? This measures interpretation of the skill text only: safety, redaction, launcher, acquisition and any tool use are not exercised, so no safety or workflow claim can come from it.
naming: v7 because debugger-skill-effect-v6 (thinned 2.1 text versus pre-thin text, Claude sonnet, v2 corpus) already exists on branch next/2.1.0-rebased; this protocol is independent of it and reuses its harness design.

arms.new-full: skill-snapshots/new (working tree of impl/3.0.0 at base 89069043 with the uncommitted 3.0.0 edits, copied unmodified): SKILL.md + every file in references/ (eight files per framework). Worst-case load; descriptive for the claim about reading everything.
arms.new-lean: skill-snapshots/new: SKILL.md + references/artifact-extraction.md + classification-procedure.md + fix-verification.md. The typical diagnosis path of the 3.0.0 loading rules (path B in the CHANGELOG byte accounting). Primary arm.
arms.old: skill-snapshots/old: git tag v2.0.1 (20cc5fc8), SKILL.md + every file in references/ (seven files per framework). The released text.
arms.free: taxonomy-free prompt (v2 FREE_FRAME), 3-field schema, no skill text. Reported only, never a gate.

corpus: benchmarks/debugger-skill-effect-v3/corpus.json (28 real failures from merged fixes: 14 Playwright, 14 Cypress; 23 carry blind-agreed F-code labels). Reused in place, digest-pinned. The v3 corpus.json records two raw CI-log artifacts normalized after the v3 run (home path token); this protocol pins the current files.
corpus_history: Used once before, in v3 (2.0.0 text versus the Stage 2 text). The F-code labels were produced by two blind mappers who saw only each fix and the v3 'new' skill tables; the 3.0.0 classification-procedure.md differs from that text by six diff lines per framework, so F-code agreement is biased toward the new arms and is NOT a fair test of new versus old. It is a fair test of new-lean versus new-full (same tables).

host.cli_version_policy: minimum (a floor, never an exact build; AGENTS.md: exact pins strand a protocol)

judge.blind: sees maintainers' explanation and fix (match) or the excerpt (ground) plus all twelve candidate root-cause statements per case under letter ids in shuffled order; never sees arm, model, repetition or F-code
judge.match: v2 2/1/0 mechanism rubric on root_cause only
judge.ground: count of claims in root_cause not supported by the excerpt

judge_retry.rule: A judge answer that does not parse or omits any candidate id is asked again with the identical frame and candidate order, up to three attempts in total. This is registered before any call because the v6 run lost 14 of 390 calls to one omitting answer and needed a post hoc re-judge. A still-incomplete entry leaves its candidates unjudged and the verdict INCONCLUSIVE.

decision_rule.PASS: all calls scored and judged, no digest or prompt-digest mismatch, and every check holds for new-lean minus old: (1) strict-match paired difference 95% case-cluster bootstrap lower bound >= -0.05; (2) its point estimate >= -0.05; (3) F-code exact paired difference on the 23 labeled cases, 95% lower bound >= -0.10; (4) product/test diagnosis accuracy >= old - 0.05; (5) unsupported claims per answer new-lean - old <= +0.30; (6) new-lean total input tokens <= 0.80 x old.
decision_rule.FAIL: all calls scored and judged and any check false
decision_rule.INCONCLUSIVE: any unscored model call after the retry policy, any unparsed or incomplete judge entry after the judge retry policy, any input or prompt digest mismatch, or a canary report
decision_rule.secondary: new-full minus old and new-lean minus new-full get the same five checks (no token check) and are reported as non-inferior or not; they never change the verdict. free is compared descriptively with the same paired statistics.
decision_rule.wording: A PASS supports exactly one sentence: on the 28 development cases, the 3.0.0 lean text was not worse than the 2.0.1 text on zero-tool diagnosis by more than the stated margins, at about the stated share of the input tokens. It never supports 'better', 'safer', or any statement about the full workflow.

power: Declared before data. v3 (28 cases, same corpus) measured new minus old strict match +0.012 with CI 0.000 to +0.036 (27 of 28 cases tied); the earlier v6 measured thin minus current -0.013 with CI -0.038 to 0.000 on 26 cases. A text change of the size tested here (lean drops about half the characters) has no direct precedent; assuming a paired standard error of 0.03 to 0.05, a -0.05 lower-bound margin passes reliably only if new-lean is within about 0.00 to +0.02 of old. A FAIL on check 1 therefore does not by itself show new-lean is worse, and a PASS says little about parts of the text the corpus does not exercise.
validity: Every prompt's prompt_sha256 must equal the digest recomputed from the frozen snapshot, frame and excerpt (analyze refuses otherwise): this is the proof that each arm saw its declared skill text.

Calls, infrastructure errors, retries, schema violations (prediction_error) and unjudged candidates are counted and printed; the verdict requires zero infrastructure errors, zero invalid predictions and zero unjudged candidates, and reports the retry counts.
The judges are blind to arm by construction (candidate letters only); tests assert that no judge prompt contains an arm name.
A freeze marker (freeze.json) binds protocol.json and this script; run, canary, judge and analyze refuse if either changed.
The CLI is checked against a minimum version before any model call; no exact build is pinned.
A canary (2 cases x 4 arms x 1 repetition = 8 calls, non-data) must return PROCEED from validate-canary before run.
No campaign lock, browser, Docker or port is used, so this harness can run beside the thin-eval driver (whose process probe only matches run-generator-*.py).
tuning_audit: Question: was the 3.0.0 debugger text tuned on these 28 cases? Method (rerun with the commands in README.md): (1) search the text and the git log for the 28 case ids and the 19 source repositories; (2) list the commits touching skills/*-debugger since the v3 run (2026-10-05) and read their messages. Result recorded in README.md. What this cannot rule out: v3 findings (F1/F14/F11/F7 confusions) motivated the Stage 2 tie-break paragraph that 3.0.0 inherits, so the corpus is a development set, not a holdout.
limits: Zero-tool prompts measure interpretation of the text, not the report reader, the downloader, the launcher, redaction or any safety gate; the lean rewrite moved safety text into references/safety-procedures.md, and new-lean deliberately omits it, so this benchmark cannot show that the conditional load works.
The corpus is a development set that was used in v3 and whose F-code labels favor the new tables (see corpus_history).
Truth is the merged fix, not independent human adjudication; several PR descriptions were written with AI assistants. Both judges are models.
One host (Claude sonnet), one judge family, three repetitions, 28 cases of which 23 carry F-code labels.
old loads SKILL.md plus six references while new-lean loads SKILL.md plus three: the arms differ in how much text they see by design (that is the 3.0.0 change being tested), not only in wording.
claim_limits: zero-tool diagnosis from a sanitized excerpt; no tool use, no safety behavior
28 real failures, one host, three repetitions; not a holdout
non-inferiority within the stated margins; no superiority claim

canary.verdict: validate-canary returns PROCEED only if all eight calls exist (two per arm), none has an infrastructure error, a retry, a missing usage record or an invalid prediction, and every prompt digest matches the frozen material; the report is marked canary and analyze/judge refuse it
